_comment: Application templates for “New website → Start from”. The catalog describes what the form offers; the installation steps are fixed code in workers/src/apps.js (an id must exist in both). Only https downloads of the vendor, verified with the vendor's published checksum.

wordpress.label: WordPress
wordpress.description: Blog and website system. Creates a PHP website with its own MariaDB database, downloads WordPress (checksum verified) and writes a wp-config.php that reads the database settings from the environment. You finish the setup in the browser.
wordpress.after: Open the website and complete the WordPress installation (language, site title, administrator account).

joomla.label: Joomla
joomla.description: Content management system. Creates a PHP website with its own MariaDB database and downloads Joomla (checksum verified against the digest of the release). You finish the setup in the browser.
joomla.after: Open the website and complete the Joomla installation. Use the values from the website's Database tab in the installer (host, database, user and the password, which you can show there). Remove the installation folder when the installer asks for it.

nextcloud.label: Nextcloud
nextcloud.description: File sync and collaboration. Creates a PHP website with its own MariaDB database, downloads Nextcloud (checksum verified) and prepares the installer so that it reads the database settings from the environment. The data directory lies outside the web root.
nextcloud.after: Open the website, choose an administrator account and finish the installation right away (the database is already filled in). Large uploads need a higher limit under PHP settings.

matomo.label: Matomo
matomo.description: Web analytics. Creates a PHP website with its own MariaDB database and downloads Matomo (checksum verified against the digest of the release). You finish the setup in the browser.
matomo.after: Open the website and complete the Matomo installation. Use the values from the website's Database tab in the installer (host, database, user and the password, which you can show there).

grav.label: Grav
grav.description: Flat-file CMS with the admin plugin: no database. Downloads Grav (checksum verified against the digest of the release). Pages are plain files you can edit in the file manager.
grav.after: Open the website and create the administrator account right away – the first visitor can do it.

uptime-kuma.label: Uptime Kuma
uptime-kuma.description: Self-hosted monitoring with a status page. Runs the official Uptime Kuma image (pinned version, nothing is downloaded at setup); its data (SQLite database, settings) lives in the file manager of the website under data.
uptime-kuma.after: Open the website and create the administrator account right away – the first visitor can do it. Choose SQLite as the database in the setup.
